assumptions.choice: Build Renko bricks from the Close price series only (standard/renko-close construction with multi-brick support per bar), rather than mixing High/Low thresholds.
assumptions.reason: Spec says 'use OHLC data to build the Renko chart' without specifying which field determines brick thresholds; Close is the conventional default source for Renko charts, and the OHLCV feed is the data being used.

assumptions.choice: Size = int(current available cash / current close price), recomputed at each entry, applied identically for both long and short entries.
assumptions.reason: Spec states 'fixed size, e.g. 100% of available capital' but is silent on exact formula and on short-side sizing; using live cash/price at entry is the most literal reading of '100% of available capital' for each new trade.

assumptions.choice: Place stop-loss and take-profit as separate Stop/Limit orders submitted only after the entry order actually fills, anchored to the executed fill price, with manual one-cancels-other bookkeeping instead of backtrader's buy_bracket/sell_bracket.
assumptions.reason: Bracket orders in backtrader compute stop/limit prices relative to the price at order-creation time, not the eventual fill price, which would misalign with the spec's 'distance ... from the entry point'.

assumptions.choice: Apply the 'last two bricks same direction' confirmation filter only to new entries, not to reversal exits.
assumptions.reason: The spec lists exit conditions separately and unconditionally ('close when a brick forms below/above the previous one'), while the trend-confirmation rule is introduced only under entry-related additional rules to filter false signals.

assumptions.choice: On a reversal brick that closes an existing position, do not evaluate a new opposite-direction entry on that same brick; a new entry requires its own subsequent two-brick confirmation.
assumptions.reason: The reversal brick by construction differs in direction from the brick before it, so it cannot itself satisfy the 'last two bricks same direction' entry filter; keeping exit and entry as separate brick events is the direct consequence of applying both stated rules together.

assumptions.choice: The first processed bar only initializes the Renko reference level (no brick, no signal); brick formation and signals begin once price first moves by one brick size from that baseline.
assumptions.reason: Spec is silent on chart initialization; a starting reference point is required before any 'previous brick' comparison is possible.
